input.summary: Add frequency, notice, business-hours, independent-auditor, cost and no-system-access limits to IBM's investigation right in § 11.3.
input.comment: [Playbook] IBM's investigation right in 11.3 is currently unlimited, unannounced and at our cost, so we have added our standard audit guardrails: once per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, an independent auditor under confidentiality, off-site review where practicable with no direct access to our systems, and IBM's cost unless an underpayment exceeds 5%. We can fall back to 15 days' notice and a 10% underpayment threshold if needed.

ops.text: Any investigation under this Subsection 11.3 that requires access to Customer's records, facilities or systems will be conducted: (i) no more than once in any twelve (12) month period; (ii) upon at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Customer; (iii) during Customer's normal business hours and in a manner that does not unreasonably disrupt Customer's business; (iv) by an independent third-party auditor bound by written confidentiality obligations no less protective than those of this Agreement; (v) remotely or off-site wherever practicable, and IBM will have no direct access to Customer systems or Customer Components; and (vi) at IBM's expense, unless the investigation reveals an underpayment by Customer exceeding five percent (5%) of the amounts due for the period reviewed, in which case Customer will reimburse IBM's reasonable costs of the investigation.
